_comment: Static project configuration. Edited by developers only; the Council maintainer never needs to touch this file.

treasury.label: DAO Treasury
treasury._indexBeforeNote: Until 2024-04-03 the Treasury ATLAS account had about one transaction a day (about 300 in total), so that part of its history is scanned once in full. From April 2024 SAGE crafting fees arrive thousands of times a day; from then on the dashboard derives them from the daily balance (see Crafting fees in the README).
treasury._indexNote: The Treasury ATLAS account receives ~20k fee transfers a day, so it is not scanned. Its outflows are still captured through the wallet, which signs every payout.

oldTreasury.label: Initial DAO Treasury
oldTreasury._note: The Treasury before the multisig (Dec 2021 to May 2023). Its funds moved to the DAO Treasury on 16 May 2023; it is empty since and kept for its history.

_councilMultisigsNote: The Council's Squads multisig accounts (not their vaults). Their transactions per month form the on-chain Council activity chart. Treasury and Fund: read from their own transfers; the PIP multisigs: SAC-3 meeting minutes #38 (6 Oct 2026).

income._note: Inflows from a counterparty that sends at least this many transfers are summarised per month instead of listed one by one.
income._craftingToleranceNote: Health flag when a month's crafting fees differ from the average of the months on either side by more than this share. 0.25 caught a hidden 10M transfer in a test while flagging none of the 30 real months.

sheet._idNote: Council test setup: a copy of the sheet. The Council's real sheet is 1QWkFjcLwhw4GHqk5Stz72H3WRwIb52f-UDnKne7hTtY. When switching back, also remove testNotice.
sheet.testNotice: Test setup: this dashboard currently reads from and saves to a test copy of the Council's sheet, not the real one. Figures and notes may include test edits.
sheet._tabsNote: Each tab is a gid (digits) or a tab name. Named tabs are found automatically once they exist, including tabs created from the dashboard's editor.

editing._note: Two-way editing between the dashboard and the sheet. Off while googleClientId is empty. The client ID is public by design (it identifies the app, it grants nothing); access is decided by each editor's own permissions on the sheet.

documents._note: PDF documents on payouts (invoices, receipts). Only the owner account can upload; the files go into a folder of that name in its Google Drive and stay private there. Empty owner = no uploads.

youtube._note: The Council's channel. Its public feed is read on every build (no key). A video is a meeting when its title says Meeting (or names a term, CT-4 / Term #4). What was discussed comes from the minutes in the sheet's Meeting minutes tab; PIPs named there (PIP-36) link the meeting to that proposal.

rpc._note: RPC_URL (env) is used for balances and transaction lookups; any provider works. SIGNATURES_RPC_URL (env) is used to list each address's transaction history and MUST be archive-complete: some commercial RPCs silently return gaps there. The public endpoint is complete.

daoRules._note: DAO rules the dashboard calculates with. Only a passed PIP changes them: add a new version with the day the PIP passed as 'from' (keep the older versions, past figures are calculated with the rules of their time). The Ecosystem Fund page lists the rules in force. pipLimitBasis: 'initialFunding' = % of the fund's balance after its first funding; 'lastRefill' = % of the fund's balance after the latest refill, until the next refill.

fund.title: Refresh of PIP-4 the Ecosystem Fund
fund._refillDatesNote: PIP-23 writes 'Mar 31, Jun 20, Sep 30, and Dec 31'; read as the quarter ends (Jun 30).

foundation.title: Star Atlas Foundation
foundation._note: A recurring annual budget of no more than 100,000 USD from the Treasury for the Foundation's operations and maintenance; anything beyond needs a DAO vote in advance.

budget._note: Budget page settings. windowMonths: complete months the averages use. foundationCategories: payout labels (cost categories) that count against the Foundation's yearly budget. projectRefills: how many upcoming refill dates the projection shows.
